latest_release.body:
This is the second maintenance release of the 2026.02 stable line. It contains bug fixes, robustness improvements, and security patches backported to the [stable/2026.02](https://github.com/EVerest/EVerest/tree/stable/2026.02) branch.

In line with the [project's release strategy](https://everest.github.io/nightly/project/releases/releases-and-versioning.html), this patch release does not introduce breaking changes to the public API.

## Upgrade Notes

Several security fixes tighten behaviour that a deployment may rely on:

- OCPP: incoming websocket messages are limited to 4 MiB by the new `MaxIncomingMessageSize` option (`Internal` in OCPP 1.6, `InternalCtrlr` in OCPP 2.x). A larger message closes the connection with status 1009 (Message Too Big). Fragmented websocket messages are now reassembled before they are parsed.
- OCPP 2.x: `InternalCtrlr.EnableTLSKeylog` is now ReadOnly, as it already was in OCPP 1.6.
- System: firmware downloads accept only FTP, FTPS, HTTP and HTTPS, and diagnostics uploads additionally SFTP. A firmware URL without a scheme is downloaded over HTTPS.
- evse_security: private key files and their directories are restricted to the owner.
- Framework: RFC 3339 timestamps are validated strictly, so malformed timestamps that were accepted before are now rejected.

## Changes since 2026.02.1

### APIs

- powermeter: add an optional `capabilities` var reporting the minimum export/import current the meter can measure within its accuracy class; EvseManager applies it as DC minimum current limit by @Pietfried
- Fix inconsistencies in the AsyncAPI specs for EVerestAPI by @cburandt
- slac_API: align the AsyncAPI spec with the implementation by @Pietfried
- slac_API: fix the documentation not matching the enum name by @marcemmers

### Hardware Drivers

- LemDCBM400600: publish minimum current capabilities by @Pietfried
- LemDCBM400600: reduce HTTP and polling overhead by @djchhp

## Notable Bug Fixes

### Core

- EvseManager: handle unplug, disable and fatal errors in timed charger states by @corneliusclaussen
- EvseManager: fix a cable check race condition causing permanent charger inoperability by @rishabhvaish
- EvseManager: do not raise a cable check fault on a requested transaction stop by @florinmihut
- EvseManager: refresh the Inoperative error when the set of active fatal causes changes by @biubiuzhang
- EvseManager: make `SessionLog::output()` thread-safe by @biubiuzhang
- EvseManager: do not reset CP state F on BSP state events by @Pietfried
- EvseManager: request energy again after a pause by the EVSE by @Pietfried
- EvseManager: do not divide by 0 when the UK random delay maximum is 0 by @hikinggrass
- EvseManager: avoid `bad_optional_access` on a negative max current by @mlitre
- Auth: publish Withdrawn for granted authorizations by @Pietfried
- Auth: check the requested EVSE in `reservation_exists` by @Pietfried
- Auth: correctly map EVSE ids to EvseManagers for reservations by @hikinggrass
- Auth: check `evse_ids` against the selected EVSE by @hikinggrass
- Auth: clear the withdraw request after it is handled by @hikinggrass
- Auth: release tokens resolved as already in process by @hikinggrass
- Auth: only notify known EVSEs for rejected tokens by @hikinggrass
- ErrorHistory: bind error filter values in SQL queries by @hikinggrass
- System: use SIGTERM instead of SIGINT for the System module reset by @Pietfried
- System: restrict firmware download and diagnostics upload protocols by @hikinggrass
- Linux_Systemd_Rauc: do not use `eval` for the diagnostics collector options by @hikinggrass

### Framework

- Keep malformed messages on internal and external MQTT topics from terminating a module or the manager (partial backport) by @hikinggrass
- Do not grant `CAP_CHOWN` to modules that request other capabilities by @hikinggrass
- Add strict RFC 3339 timestamp validation by @hikinggrass
- libio: harden mDNS packet parsing against malformed packet

[![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org/projects/6739/badge)](https://bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org/projects/6739)

# EVerest

EVerest is a [Linux Foundation Energy](https://lfenergy.org/) backed open-source modular
framework for setting up a full stack environment for EV charging. The modular
software architecture fosters customizablility and lets you configure your
dedicated charging station based on interchangeable modules. All communication
is performed by the lightweight and flexible MQTT message queueing service.
EVerest will help to speed the adoption to e-mobility by utilizing all the
open-source advantages for the EV charging world. It will also enable new
features for local energy management, PV-integration and many more!

# Main Features

- Modular and extensible architecture
- Support for AC and DC charging
- Support for EV charging protocols
    - OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1 and OCPP 2.1
    - ISO 15118-2, -3 and -20
    - IEC 61851
    - DIN SPEC 70121
- Ready-to-use hardware drivers for many compatible hardware components 
    - BSPs for charge controllers
    - Powermeters
    - Isolation monitors
    - DC Power supplies
    - RFID/NFC readers
    - Payment terminals
- Energy management implementations and API
- Standardized and stable APIs to allow easy integrations
- Bring-up modules for custom hardware testing and integration
- Ensured standards compliance
- OTA service to keep EV chargers up-to-date
- Security best practices following OpenSSF
- ISO / IEC 5230 open source license compliance
- Secure communication channels through TPM
- Yocto support for custom embedded Linux images

# Getting Started

See our documentation on [everest.github.io](https://everest.github.io) to get started with using or developing EVerest. The best
way to start is with our [Getting Started Guides](https://everest.github.io/nightly/how-to-guides/getting-started/index.html).

# Community

Find more information about the community and ways to get involved [here](https://everest.github.io/nightly/project/community.html).

# Contributing to EVerest

Anyone can contribute to EVerest! Learn more about getting involved
[here](https://everest.github.io/nightly/project/contributing.html).

# Background

The EVerest project was initiated by PIONIX GmbH to help with the
electrification of the mobility sector.
